acceptance.text: after `python3 -m hello_loop.migrate` on a fresh database, table `bookmarks` exists with columns `id` (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY), `url` (TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE), `title` (TEXT NOT NULL) and `created_at` (TEXT NOT NULL), and nothing else
running `python3 -m hello_loop.migrate` a second time succeeds and `schema_migrations` holds `0001_create_bookmarks` exactly once
`python3 -m hello_loop.migrate --down` removes the `bookmarks` table and its `schema_migrations` row (this is the item's down migration)
`python3 -m hello_loop.seed` inserts exactly 3 sample bookmarks; running it twice still leaves exactly 3 rows
`tests/test_schema.py` exists, covers AC-F1-1 to AC-F1-4, and passes under `verify_tests`

intent: Add the bookmarks table as the first migration (with its down migration) and a seed command that loads three sample bookmarks. Everything else reads and writes this table.
title: Bookmarks schema, migration and seed
